first_impression.reaction: Every other result for this search says 'September!' and shows the same Oia sunset. This one opens with 'any guide that names one month for every couple is guessing' and then gives me the four things that actually decide it: island, heat, church or not, and how long everyone stays. That's honest, and it's the way James and I already think about it. No 'fairytale', no 'dream day'. I kept reading.

journey.quote: The months that work for you depend on four things: the island, how well your guests cope with heat, whether you want a church ceremony, and how long everyone will stay.
journey.reaction: Good framing. Half our guests are flying in from overseas and his grandparents are in their eighties, so 'how well your guests cope with heat' is the right question, not just what looks best in photos.

journey.section: How to read the weather figures
journey.quote: The Rodos and Heraklion figures cover 1955 to 2010, Chania Souda covers 1958 to 2010 and Kerkyra covers 1955 to 2010.
journey.reaction: I'm a lawyer and even I skimmed this. I believe the numbers. I just don't need the data periods before I've seen the table. This is where my eyes started sliding.

journey.section: How to read the weather figures
journey.quote: HNMS has no station on Santorini, Mykonos or Paros. Naxos, at 3 metres above sea level, is the official station for the group, so figures here are labelled Naxos.
journey.reaction: That's actually useful. I'd have assumed every site's 'Santorini weather' figure was measured on Santorini. Quietly honest.

journey.section: Greece wedding weather by month, April to October
journey.quote: Each cell shows the average maximum temperature, then the average number of rain days.
journey.reaction: The table is the reason I'd bookmark this. One screen, five islands, seven months. I'd screenshot it for Mum.

journey.section: Greece wedding weather by month, April to October
journey.quote: June to August is the dry core everywhere except Corfu, which keeps three to five rain days a month through summer.
journey.reaction: Didn't know Corfu was the exception. That's exactly the kind of trade-off I want flagged before we fall for a villa.

journey.quote: Evenings are cool. Naxos averages a minimum of 12.5°C and Chania Souda 11.4°C, so an outdoor dinner needs wraps, heaters or a room to move into.
journey.reaction: Practical, not preachy. That's the sort of thing a planner should tell you and most don't until the night.

journey.quote: For a July wedding, that shapes the day: an evening ceremony, shade for the aperitivo, water at every seat, and shorter excursions for older guests.
journey.reaction: This is the line that speaks to our biggest worry. It turns the heat warning into an actual plan for the day.

journey.quote: Smartraveller notes that ferry services can be delayed or cancelled in bad weather, mainly because of strong winds, so reconfirm departures.
journey.reaction: Our friends will absolutely try to island-hop in. Good, but it also makes me think: who's reconfirming the ferries for 40 international guests? Not me, I hope.

journey.quote: The Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of Australia lists 1 to 15 August (the Dormition of the Theotokos) and 29 August among the dates when marriages are not permitted.
journey.reaction: James's yiayia would want a church wedding if we chose Greece. I had no idea mid-August was closed. That alone justifies the read.

journey.section: The Cyclades: Santorini, Mykonos and Paros
journey.quote: On Santorini, Santo Wines in Pyrgos says its Wine Tourism Center, beside the winery with a view over the volcano, is open all year round.
journey.reaction: Wait, is that a wedding venue or just a cellar door? Everywhere else the venue windows are about weddings. This one reads like a tourism opening-hours line and I'm not sure what it tells me about getting married there.

journey.quote: At Angsana Corfu, outdoor spaces run from April or mid-May to the end of September or October, depending on the space.
journey.reaction: Fourth or fifth time Angsana Corfu has come up. Helpful once, but it starts to feel like the only venue they checked, and we're not even leaning towards Corfu.

journey.quote: **Older guests, or anyone who struggles in heat.** May and late September to October keep maximums in the low to mid 20s at most stations.
journey.reaction: This section is what I'd actually send to the family group chat. Scenarios instead of a 'best month' verdict, and ours is right there.

journey.quote: Ask your venue about water temperature for your month, since the figures in this guide cover air, not sea.
journey.reaction: Bit of a dodge. If you can't answer the question, don't put it in the FAQ. The air minimums are a non-answer to 'when can people swim'.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact, matching your shortlisted months to venue availability, travel and guest stays, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: AUD and the fee in writing hit my hidden-cost fear directly. 'Single point of contact' is what I want after reading about ferries and heat plans. Calm, not pushy.

unanswered_questions: When do guests actually want to swim, and what's the sea like in June versus September?
If our guests are island-hopping in, does our Wedded Advisor reconfirm ferries and move people if a sailing is cancelled, or is that on us?
Is the Santo Wines space on Santorini actually available for weddings year round, or is that just the tasting centre?
Can you show us a real wedding in Greece with the venue and the month, so we can see how the heat or wind plan worked on the day?
Does the Wedded Advisor liaise with a priest in Greece on Orthodox dates, or do we do that through our own parish?
would_share_with: James: the four-factor intro and the 'Which months suit your wedding' scenarios
Mum and Dad (contributing): the weather table, so they stop assuming July is ideal
James's parents: the Orthodox closed dates, before anyone suggests the August long weekend

cta_reaction.quote: Once you have two or three months in mind, a [Wedded Concierge consultation](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=best-time-to-get-married-in-greece&utm_content=primary) turns them into dates a venue can actually hold.
cta_reaction.why: It's the right ask at the right moment: once we've got a shortlist, not before. AUD quotes and a fee in writing take the edge off my currency and hidden-cost worries. But we haven't picked Greece yet, and I'd want to read an island guide and see one real wedding with a venue and date before I hand over our details.

top_3_changes: In 'How to read the weather figures', cut or move the data-period sentence ('The Rodos and Heraklion figures cover 1955 to 2010...') below the table, and keep the useful Naxos-for-the-Cyclades note above it. Right now the dry station detail sits between a great intro and the table I actually came for, and it reads more like an almanac than a luxury planner.

In 'The Cyclades', either say whether Santo Wines' space takes weddings in each season or drop 'its Wine Tourism Center ... is open all year round'. As written it's a tourism opening-hours line in a wedding-season guide, and it makes me question what the other venue windows mean. Fewer repeat mentions of Angsana Corfu would also stop it feeling like a one-venue sample.

In the FAQ, 'When does the sea warm up for guests?' answers with air minimums. Either answer the swimming question plainly or say it isn't published and goes on the venue checklist, otherwise remove the question.
